findings.evidence: Lines 136-143. The core scientific contract has a literal composition hole. §4.5 force-flats every position at rollover_instant − 300 s, so the buffer window is [rollover−300s, rollover). §4.7's entry ban covers only 'the 30 minutes preceding the buffer window' = [rollover−2100s, rollover−300s]. An entry at t inside the buffer window itself, e.g., rollover−100s, is not literally forbidden by §4.7, and §4.6's 'any entry whose forced exit would land inside the buffer window is forbidden by construction' is ambiguous for such t: no force-flat time exists at or after the window opens (rollover−300s is in the past), so the 'forced exit' of such an entry is undefined by the plan's own terms — it cannot be shown to close before rollover. This is the exact clause the rollover-flat structural claim (D2-2, §7.6) rides on. The directive's 'every position must close BEFORE rollover' would be violated by the literal text, not just by a buggy implementation.
findings.required_fix: Replace with a closed-form entry constraint, e.g.: 'An entry is permitted only at t such that t < rollover_instant − 300 s AND t + max_hold <= next rollover_instant − 300 s; entries at any t >= rollover_instant − 300 s are forbidden (the position could not be flat by the buffer boundary). D2-2 must include a fixture with an attempted entry inside the buffer window and must assert the contract rejects it.'
